ARM and PowerPC are both more efficient architectures than x86, but Windows and Intel have a major influence on our hardware. Microsoft "tried" ARM in a way they should have known it was going to fail. Windows created a walled garden system they called Windows RT. Windows on ARM could have been great, had they ported the Win32 system to work with it and not lock it down. There are two reasons MS could have decided to do this.

  1. MS wants to control all the apps and thought that since "ARM is the future" they could get away with using their name to become the draconian dictator that is the Apple App Store.

  2. MS has a deal with Intel, and wanted to make sure ARM on the desktop would never become a thing. MS knew any kind of walled garden Windows OS would be a big flop, but to please investors that expect MS to enter the tablet space, they created Windows RT to be a decoy to destroy the idea of ARM on the Desktop.

So now MS has completely dropped ARM support on Windows. Their plan worked. But we still have Linux to save the day, right?

WRONG!

All these ARM Linux boxes that they have on the market to "behave like a PC" have terrible hardware, for example the Raspberry Pi. AFAIK, there is currently no way to have these ARM Linux boxes interface with modern GPUs like Nvidia Geforce or AMD Radeon.

BUT WHAT ABOUT AMD?

AMD licenses Intel technology, so we have the illusion of choice. Fact is, all x86 (or x86-64) processors are a part of the "Wintel" monopoly.

BUT THERE IS HOPE!

MS has actually given us an opportunity to get away from the future ARM monopoly.

We need to create a powerful new standard under the public domain and build capable computers that can interface with today's modern GPUs and play modern games with a good selection.

The problem with having multiple CPU architectures in the PC space is that developers would have to recompile for each piece of hardware. Valve would be a good company to kickstart something like this. If Valve were to move a significant portion of it's playerbase over to Open Hardware Steamboxes, developers would see the demand and we could get our ports. developers already has to do this step for Android and iOS development, so it would be very much possible to make the transition.

A problem I see with ARM is that Android is monopolizing the ARM space. Every ARM gaming box comes with Android. Why can't we have (at least as a start) Open Hardware gaming boxes with GNU Linux, or in the future, Haiku (I think we need an OS that started from scratch in the modern age to fully utilize our hardware eventually). ARM is a new standard created for modern use, and in return, it is a lot more efficient, but we can do better by creating a new OS that fits together with a new CPU architecture to completely maximize power and efficiency, instead of using a standard built for cell phones made for looking at twitter.

BUT ARM IS STILL A STEP IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION

ARM is all we have right now in the alternative CPU space. At least many more companies are making ARM despite licensing costs going to ARM themselves. I would be pleased if a new CPU standard arises today using open plans for any manufacturer to use free of charge and Public Domain IP so no one company has control over the entire industry. This is tough, and likely expensive, but it has to be done for the future of computing hardware. x86 legacy is holding us back and is wasting tons of electricity every day. The transition won't be easy, but the day we have this new standard in place, competition in PC hardware would flourish so we can truly have our PC master race instead of this locked down standard that borders on console setups. New open GPU standards could finally break the AMD-Nvidia monopoly and we could finally end up with new companies that make better cards cheaper with better energy efficiency. A goldmine for bitcoin miners in its early days, but a massive increase in innovation over a much shorter period.
